consensus_summary: All responses identify the primary meaning of bread as Jesus Christ Himself (the Bread of Life) and His body in the Eucharist/Lord’s Supper, with manna as typology; common alternatives include the Word of God, daily provision, and fellowship/unity.
consensus_core_identification: Jesus Christ as the Bread of Life and eucharistic body
boundary_disagreement: Book excludes the dominant christological/eucharistic sense (and other common layers) entirely, restricting the symbol solely to the Word-of-God sense.
material_contradiction: Consensus primary referent is Christ; book’s sole referent is the word of God (a secondary alternative in consensus). Both cannot be the core identification of the same symbol.
rationale: Consensus cores (across A–D) are uniformly christological/eucharistic on the basis of John 6 and the Last Supper texts, treating the Deut 8:3/Matt 4:4 Word-of-God sense as a distinct common alternative. The book replaces that settled primary referent with the alternative alone. This is replacement of the central identification, not boundary adjustment around the same referent.
strongest_objection: Book’s identification omits the NT texts that establish the consensus primary meaning of bread as Christ.
